messages:
Marta Chen: Heads-up — follow-up from the render-graph RFC. Seeing 95th+ p99 tails on dashboard load that line up with large hydration jobs and cross-tenant cache churn.
Samir Patel: Repro'd locally with recent nightly trace. It looks like the hydration pass does a lot of fan-in queries when the view graph has shared subtrees.
Lia Nguyen: Are we sure it's shared subtree lookups rather than serialization hotpaths? I instrumented the serializer and it's fine.
Samir Patel: +1, serializer seems ok. The hotspots are multiple small queries that all touch the same backing tables — cache eviction churn. Sharding the cache by logical view could help.
Marta Chen: Proposed follow-up: split the render-graph into two runtime surfaces — a readonly "query orchard" that materializes stable subviews (long-lived cache), and a readonly/ephemeral "render spine" that composes materialized nodes. Contracts: materialized nodes expose a stable key and TTL; render spine gets only key references.
Noah: That sounds reasonable. Tradeoffs: extra write path to maintain materializations, storage cost, and eventual staleness window. SLO impact? p50 ok, p95 improve, p99 unknown until we simulate.
Aisha: For rollout we should keep both modes live: a feature flag per tenant + canary. If the materializer fails, fall back to old path. Also need metrics: materialization hit rate, write lag, evictions, and end-to-end load latency.
Marta Chen: Agreed. Sketch of feature flag config:
```yaml
feature_flags:
  render_graph_mode: hybrid # options: legacy | hybrid | materialized
  materializer_ttl_seconds: 300
  materializer_batch_size: 128
```
Samir Patel: Implementation notes: materializer will be async, driven by the same executor used for background prefetch. It should prioritize cold nodes and use adaptive batching based on queue depth.
Lia Nguyen: Question on RBAC: materialized nodes may contain tenant-sensitive aggregates. We must ensure materializer enforces per-tenant encryption and respects row-level filters. Can't leak cross-tenant cached blobs.
Marta Chen: Good call — materializer must sign blobs with tenant key and include tenant_id in the cache key namespace. Add KMS annotation to schema. Also add an access check in read path.
DevInfra Bot: deploy:render-materializer v0.1 deployed to staging at 2026-03-21T15:12:03Z :rocket:
Samir Patel: Can we add a canary pipeline that routes 1% traffic to materialized path for a small set of non-critical tenants? We'll watch hit rate and latencies for 48h.
Aisha: I'll own canary. Plan: enable hybrid for ten small tenants, monitor metrics, run load tests with bench-tool, and schedule cutover playbook if 99th latency improves without error regression.
Marta Chen: Thanks — follow-ups: (1) infra to add tenant namespacing to cache keys (Samir), (2) security to confirm KMS workflow (Lia), (3) Aisha to run canary and report in 48h. I'll open RFC postmortem thread once we have canary results.
Samir Patel: noted. I'll push a PR with keygen and basic metrics today.
Lia Nguyen: I'll ping security for KMS review. :eyes:
Aisha: Canary scheduled for tomorrow 10:00 PT. I'll drop the results in #eng-platform.
Marta Chen: cool — thanks all :thumbsup:
